lesson.text: Quick memory: how long should children be active each day? (At least 60 minutes.) Being active in the day also helps you sleep well at night.
Children your age need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep every night. Sleep is not wasted time: your body grows and mends itself while you sleep.
Sleep helps your brain too. It sorts out what you learned today and stores it as memories. After a good sleep, it is easier to think, learn and feel calm.
Too little sleep can make you grumpy, clumsy and slow to learn. It makes it harder to get along with other people.
Work out your sleep: from 8 pm to midnight is 4 hours, then from midnight to 7 am is 7 more. 4 + 7 = 11 hours of sleep.
A good bedtime routine: the same bedtime every night, and screens off an hour before bed. Have a bath or a wash, brush your teeth, then read a calm story in bed.
Make your bedroom a sleep place: dark, quiet and not too warm. Fizzy or sugary drinks and big meals late in the evening make it harder to fall asleep.
Try it in the world: build a cosy bedroom with a bed, a lamp and dark curtains of wool. Then plan your real bedtime routine with a grown-up: what will you do at each step?

exercises.prompt: About how many hours of sleep do children your age need each night?
exercises.hint: It is most of the night, but not most of the whole day.
exercises.explain: Children of 8 or 9 need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep each night.

exercises.prompt: Your body grows and mends itself while you sleep.
exercises.explain: True: while you sleep, your body grows and repairs itself.

choices: a calm routine and a dark, quiet room
a fast game just before bed
exercises.explain: A calm routine, and a dark, quiet room, help your body get ready for sleep.

exercises.prompt: It is best to switch screens off about an hour before bed.
exercises.hint: Do bright screens make you sleepy?
exercises.explain: True: bright screens keep your brain awake, so switch them off an hour before bed.

exercises.prompt: Tilly goes to bed at 8 pm and wakes up at 7 am. How many hours does she sleep?
exercises.hint: Count the hours to midnight, then the hours after midnight.
exercises.explain: 8 pm to midnight is 4 hours, midnight to 7 am is 7 hours: 4 + 7 = 11 hours.

exercises.prompt: Bram sleeps from 9 pm to 7 am. How many hours is that?
exercises.hint: Count the hours to midnight first.
exercises.explain: 9 pm to midnight is 3 hours, midnight to 7 am is 7 hours: 3 + 7 = 10 hours.

exercises.prompt: Put a bedtime routine in order.
exercises.hint: Screens go off an hour before bed; lights go out last.
items: have a bath or a wash
exercises.explain: Screens off, a bath or wash, brush your teeth, a calm story, then lights out.

exercises.prompt: Which is a sign of not getting enough sleep?
exercises.hint: How do you feel when you are very tired?
choices: feeling full of energy all day
exercises.explain: Too little sleep makes it hard to concentrate, and you may feel grumpy or clumsy.

exercises.prompt: What does your brain do while you sleep?
exercises.hint: Why is it easier to remember things after sleep?
choices: sorts and stores what you learned
exercises.explain: Your brain sorts out the day and stores what you learned as memories.

exercises.prompt: Zara must wake up at 7 am and needs 10 hours of sleep. When should she be asleep?
exercises.hint: Count back from 7 am: first to midnight, then the rest.
exercises.explain: 7 am back to midnight is 7 hours; 3 more hours back is 9 pm. 7 + 3 = 10 hours.

exercises.prompt: Mimi keeps waking up tired. Her tablet is on in bed until late. What should she try first?
exercises.hint: What keeps the brain awake at night?
choices: switching screens off an hour before bed
exercises.explain: Switching screens off an hour before bed helps her brain get ready for sleep.

exercises.prompt: Does it help sleep, or make it harder?
exercises.hint: Which ones are calm, dark and quiet?
exercises.explain: Helps: a dark room, a warm bath, reading. Makes it harder: a loud television, a fizzy drink, a bright screen.

exercises.prompt: Being active during the day can help you sleep better at night.
exercises.hint: How do you feel after a busy day?
exercises.explain: True: being active in the day helps you fall asleep and sleep well.

exercises.prompt: Bram went to bed at 7:30 pm and woke at 6:30 am. How many hours did he sleep?
exercises.hint: Count the whole hours from 7:30 pm to 12:30 am, then on to 6:30 am.
exercises.explain: 7:30 pm to 12:30 am is 5 hours, then to 6:30 am is 6 more: 5 + 6 = 11 hours.
